testcase.name: a member sits on its true spot at progress 0 and on its ring place at 1
the ring of eight is as tight as square touch areas allow - its radius is derived, not a round number
a spiral's markers are all distinct
the first marker of a ring is straight above the spot
just under the stacking distance is a stack on either axis, and the stacking distance is 26
a spiral of nine to sixty leaves no two touch squares overlapping and clears the spot
a ring of two to eight leaves no two touch squares overlapping
a chain is not a stack - a marker that overlaps only a neighbour of the tapped one is left out
overlap needs both axes - a marker far above is not in the stack
progress moves the places a touch is tested against
a ring is a circle about the stack's own spot, a touch size or more from it
the tapped marker is not counted twice when the query returned it too
more than eight are a spiral, not a ring of the same radius
a single marker still gets a real offset, never NaN
where two squares would both contain a touch the nearer marker wins
at exactly the stacking distance apart it is not a stack
a touch anywhere in a fanned marker's own 48 dp square finds it, and outside does not
two markers under the stacking distance apart are a stack, and the tapped one comes first
